episode_title: Multifamily’s Boom, Crash, and the Strategy for What Comes Next

real_qa.q: What happened to multifamily property values when the Federal Reserve raised interest rates 550 basis points between 2022 and 2023?
real_qa.r: Multifamily values started to compress or cap rates started to expand. From 2022 onward, anyone who bought in 2021 saw those properties suffer. Values dropped 20 to 30 percent on multifamily across the country. This occurred because when debt becomes more expensive, buyers can only afford lower-priced properties, forcing values downward to accommodate higher interest rates.

real_qa.q: Why did multifamily investors use floating rate debt during the low interest rate period instead of locking in fixed rates?
real_qa.r: Investors used floating rate debt because it offered even cheaper terms initially than fixed rates at 3 or 4 percent. They wanted to outbid competitors on property prices and felt they could compete better with floating rates, even though they were excited and wanted to play in the market. This strategy backfired when rates rose dramatically.

real_qa.q: How many apartment units is Kansas City behind on development since the 2008 crash?
real_qa.r: Kansas City is 18,000 apartment units behind on development from 2008 to now. This shortage occurred because after the 2008 crisis, people were unwilling and unable to borrow money to build new multifamily properties, creating a long-term supply constraint that compounded over the next decade.
real_qa.requete: Kansas City 18000 apartment units shortage development

real_qa.q: What was the national housing shortage across all residential real estate following the 2008 financial crisis?
real_qa.r: Nationally, there is around 4 million housing units short. This shortage dates all the way back to the crash and reflects the fact that after the 2008 crisis, people were reluctant to borrow money and build new housing, and that gap has never been fully closed.

real_qa.q: What percentage of new apartment deliveries during the boom cycle were concentrated in Sunbelt markets?
real_qa.r: Approximately 70 percent of all new apartments delivered were in the Sunbelt area, specifically in markets like Dallas, Austin, Phoenix, and Florida. This concentration occurred because investors followed the narrative that these markets had the highest growth and lowest cap rates, exacerbating the overbuild problem.
real_qa.requete: 70 percent apartments Sunbelt Dallas Austin Phoenix

guest.bio_context: Aaron has been investing in real estate since 2005, starting with small multifamily properties and progressing to larger assets over the last 8-10 years. He has experience navigating multiple real estate cycles and currently works with sponsors and equity providers in the multifamily space, actively sourcing and underwriting new deals.
